accepted.s: The standard explanation for the weak revenue position of municipalities is:
o: Chronic under-assessment and under-collection of property tax
accepted.x: Municipalities are weakened particularly by chronic under-assessment and under-collection of property tax.
accepted.tq: Identify the principal cause behind weak municipal finances.
accepted.sec: Own revenue of local bodies - property tax and others

accepted.s: The Economic Survey 2016-17 used satellite imagery to estimate the gap between actual and potential property tax in:
accepted.x: The Economic Survey 2016-17 measured the actual-potential property-tax gap in Bengaluru and Jaipur using satellite imagery.
accepted.tq: Test the precise city pair associated with a quantitative assessment method.
accepted.sec: Own revenue of local bodies - property tax and others

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly classified as a non-tax revenue source of urban local bodies?
o: User charges for water and sanitation
accepted.x: Rent, fees and fines, royalties, interest and user charges are non-tax revenues; water and sanitation charges are examples of user charges.
accepted.tq: Separate tax revenue from non-tax revenue by classification.
accepted.sec: Own revenue of local bodies - property tax and others

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the revenue sources of urban local bodies:
1. Professional tax and advertisement tax are tax revenue sources.
2. Rents, fees and fines are non-tax revenue sources.
3. Loans from State or financial institutions may finance capital works.
4. Municipal bonds are widely used by all urban local bodies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Professional and advertisement taxes are tax revenues; rents, fees and fines are non-tax revenues; and loans may finance capital works. Municipal bonds are used only in a few large cities, so statement 4 is false.
accepted.tq: Find the overbroad statement in a classification question.
accepted.sec: Own revenue of local bodies - property tax and others

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Devolution — State funds to municipalities on SFC recommendation
Loans — Routine payment of municipal salaries only
accepted.x: Loans from the State or financial institutions are used for capital works, not restricted to routine salary payments. The other pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the incorrectly described function of a revenue source.
accepted.sec: Own revenue of local bodies - property tax and others

accepted.s:
Which of the following reform measures is associated with improving the property-tax base and municipal finance?
1. Using SVAMITVA drone maps to provide panchayats with a property-tax baseline
2. Incentivising property-tax reform under AMRUT 2.0
3. Encouraging municipal bonds under AMRUT 2.0
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: SVAMITVA drone maps can create a property-tax baseline, while AMRUT 2.0 incentivises property-tax reform and municipal bonds.
accepted.tq: Use the ‘all of the above’ option when all listed reform levers are supported.
accepted.sec: Own revenue of local bodies - property tax and others

accepted.s: Octroi, in the context of local finance, was:
o: A performance grant of the Central Finance Commission
A grant from the State Finance Commission
A fee collected only from municipal employees
accepted.x: Octroi was a traditional levy associated with local revenue.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of a historically used local levy.
accepted.sec: Own revenue of local bodies - property tax and others

accepted.s: Gram panchayats may levy which of the following, subject to authorisation by the State?
accepted.x: Gram panchayats levy only State-authorised taxes, including taxes on local fairs, house or property tax, fees and tolls. Sales tax and land revenue are State levies.
accepted.tq: Distinguish panchayat levies from State-level taxes.
accepted.sec: Panchayat revenue sources

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a direct source of revenue for panchayats?
accepted.x: NABARD is not identified as a direct source of panchayat revenue, whereas the other three are listed sources.
accepted.tq: Use the exception to separate a named institution from actual panchayat revenue sources.
accepted.sec: Panchayat revenue sources

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the financial position of panchayats:
1. Panchayats are constrained in their power to tax.
2. Panchayats depend substantially on grants.
3. Gram sabhas spend a larger share of their time on revenue generation than on local issues.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Panchayats are constrained in taxation and depend on grants. Gram sabhas spend about 4% of their time on revenue generation and 13% on local issues, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Reject the reversed comparison between two percentages.
accepted.sec: Panchayat revenue sources

accepted.s: The Gram sabhas spend approximately what proportion of their time on revenue generation and local issues, respectively?
accepted.x: Gram sabhas spend approximately 4% of their time on revenue generation and 13% on local issues.
accepted.tq: Test paired percentages in their correct order.
accepted.sec: Panchayat revenue sources

accepted.s: Which of the following committees was associated with the period 1985-88?
accepted.x: The National Commission on Urbanisation was associated with the period 1985-88.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of the committee-period association.
accepted.sec: Committees on local finance - period

accepted.s: Who was the Chairman of the Rural-Urban Relationship Committee?
accepted.x: A.P. Jain chaired the Rural-Urban Relationship Committee.
accepted.tq: Test the person associated with a named committee.
accepted.sec: Committees on local finance - period

accepted.s: Which Article enables the State Legislature to authorise Panchayats to levy, collect and appropriate taxes, duties, tolls and fees?
accepted.x: Article 243H concerns the taxation powers and financial resources of Panchayats.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related constitutional Articles.
accepted.sec: Articles 243H, 243I, 243X, 243Y - taxation powers and SFC

accepted.s: Article 243X relates primarily to:
o: The taxation powers and financial resources of Municipalities
The review of municipal finances by the Central Finance Commission
The constitution of the State Finance Commission for Panchayats
The appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor General
accepted.x: Article 243X provides the enabling framework for taxation and financial resources of Municipalities.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the parallel municipal provision from the panchayat provision.
accepted.sec: Articles 243H, 243I, 243X, 243Y - taxation powers and SFC

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 243I provides for constitution of a State Finance Commission for Panchayats.
2. The Governor constitutes the State Finance Commission within one year of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment and thereafter every five years.
3. Article 243Y provides that the State Finance Commission also reviews municipal finances.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Articles 243I and 243Y together provide for the State Finance Commission’s role regarding Panchayats and Municipalities, including its constitution and periodic review.
accepted.tq: Combine parallel constitutional provisions before selecting the code.
accepted.sec: Articles 243H, 243I, 243X, 243Y - taxation powers and SFC

accepted.s: In Article 243H, the word ‘may’ indicates that:
o: The State Legislature has an enabling power and is not compelled to impose the taxes
Only the Union Parliament can authorise local taxation
Panchayats can impose taxes without State authorisation
The State Legislature is constitutionally compelled to impose every listed tax
accepted.x: The use of ‘may’ makes the provision enabling rather than compulsory; the State Legislature may authorise the levy, collection and appropriation of the listed revenues.
accepted.tq: Interpret the legal effect of the precise constitutional word.
accepted.sec: Articles 243H, 243I, 243X, 243Y - taxation powers and SFC

accepted.s: Under Article 280(3)(bb) and (c), the Central Finance Commission suggests measures to augment the State Consolidated Fund for local bodies on the basis of recommendations made by:
accepted.x: The Central Finance Commission makes such recommendations on the basis of State Finance Commission recommendations.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct recommending body in a constitutional relationship.
accepted.sec: Articles 243H, 243I, 243X, 243Y - taxation powers and SFC

accepted.s: The State Finance Commission is constituted by the Governor:
o: Only once after each general election
accepted.x: The Governor constitutes the State Finance Commission every fifth year.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of the constitutional periodicity.
accepted.sec: State Finance Commission - constitution, tenure, AP

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a recommendation ordinarily made by a State Finance Commission?
o: Division of taxes, duties, tolls and fees between the State and local bodies
Grants-in-aid from the State Consolidated Fund
Measures to improve the finances of local bodies
Appointment of the Governor of the State
accepted.x: A State Finance Commission recommends fiscal devolution, grants-in-aid and measures to improve local finances; it does not appoint the Governor.
accepted.tq: Find the authority function that does not belong to the Commission.
accepted.sec: State Finance Commission - constitution, tenure, AP

accepted.s: Which legislation gives effect to Article 243I for Panchayats in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The Andhra Pradesh Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2005
The Andhra Pradesh Land Revenue Act, 1990
The Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994
The Andhra Pradesh Municipal Corporations Act, 1955
accepted.x: Part VI of the Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 gives effect to Article 243I for Panchayats.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional provision with its State-level implementing law.
accepted.sec: State Finance Commission - constitution, tenure, AP

accepted.s: The Panchayats Extension to Scheduled Areas Act, 1996 applies in Andhra Pradesh to:
o: All municipal corporations in coastal districts
accepted.x: PESA 1996 applies in Andhra Pradesh’s Fifth Schedule agency areas.
accepted.tq: Test the geographical scope of a special legislation.
accepted.sec: State Finance Commission - constitution, tenure, AP

accepted.s: Under the Fourteenth Finance Commission’s local-body grant formula, the weights assigned to population and area were respectively:
accepted.x: The Fourteenth Finance Commission assigned 90% weight to population based on the 2011 Census and 10% to area.
accepted.tq: Test the exact relative weights in a formula-based question.

accepted.s: Which of the following was an entry condition for urban local bodies to receive the relevant Fifteenth Finance Commission grants?
o: Publication of audited accounts and notification of baseline property-tax rates
Compulsory issue of municipal bonds by every town
Transfer of land revenue powers to municipalities
accepted.x: Urban local bodies were required to publish audited accounts and notify baseline property-tax rates.
accepted.tq: Identify compliance conditions rather than general revenue measures.

accepted.s: Tied grants under the Fifteenth Finance Commission were intended to steer Panchayats towards:
accepted.x: Tied grants were directed towards water and sanitation at the Panchayat level.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of the specified purpose of tied grants.

accepted.s: According to the stated 16th Finance Commission framework for 2026-31, the total grant for local bodies is:
accepted.x: The stated 16th Finance Commission allocation for local bodies for 2026-31 is ₹7,91,493 crore.
accepted.tq: Test the exact grant amount with adjacent numerical distractors.

accepted.s: The urban share in the stated 16th Finance Commission local-body allocation is projected to rise from 36% to:
accepted.x: The urban share is projected to increase from 36% to 45%, alongside projected urbanisation of 41% by 2031.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 16th Finance Commission grant structure:
1. Basic grants constitute 80% of the grant.
2. Half of the basic grant is tied to sanitation, waste management and water.
3. Performance grants constitute 20% and are entirely untied.
4. Performance grants are split equally between local and State performance.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The stated structure provides 80% as basic grants, with 50% of those tied and 50% untied. The 20% performance grant is entirely untied and is divided equally between local and State performance.
accepted.tq: Verify each component of a grant-allocation table before choosing the complete code.
accepted.sec: Central FC local-body grants - basic vs tied, entry conditions

accepted.s: Under the stated 16th Finance Commission structure, the portion of the basic grant that is untied is:
accepted.x: The basic grant constitutes 80% of the total, and half of the basic grant is untied; therefore the untied portion within the basic grant is 50%.
accepted.tq: Read the tied-versus-untied split within a grant category rather than the total grant.
accepted.sec: Central FC local-body grants - basic vs tied, entry conditions

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT an entry condition for local bodies under the stated 16th Finance Commission framework?
o: Every local body must issue municipal bonds
Audited accounts must be published online
The local body must be properly constituted and elected
The State Finance Commission must be constituted in a timely manner
accepted.x: The entry conditions include properly constituted elected bodies, online publication of audited accounts and timely constitution of State Finance Commissions. Mandatory municipal-bond issuance is not listed as an entry condition.
accepted.tq: Find the additional requirement that is not part of the eligibility conditions.
accepted.sec: Central FC local-body grants - basic vs tied, entry conditions

accepted.s: Performance grants under the stated 16th Finance Commission framework are linked, among other things, to:
accepted.x: Performance grants require better own-source revenue and are split equally between local and State performance.
accepted.tq: Identify the incentive-compatible fiscal condition.
accepted.sec: Central FC local-body grants - basic vs tied, entry conditions

accepted.s: The special urban local-body grants for wastewater management are intended for cities with a population of:
accepted.x: The special wastewater-management grants are intended for cities with populations of 10-40 lakh, based on Census 2011.
accepted.tq: Test the exact population range attached to a special grant.
accepted.sec: Central FC local-body grants - basic vs tied, entry conditions

accepted.s:
The one-time Urbanisation Premium is associated with which of the following measures?
1. Merging peri-urban villages
2. Adopting a Rural-to-Urban Transition Policy
3. Abolishing all municipal property taxes
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The one-time Urbanisation Premium is associated with merging peri-urban villages and adopting a Rural-to-Urban Transition Policy. Abolition of all municipal property taxes is not a condition.
accepted.tq: Reject the unrelated extreme proposal while retaining the two linked urbanisation measures.
